title: Fair limits on a logistics partner API
summary: Stop one partner's bad script from taking down shipment tracking for everyone else.
context: Nandi Freight exposes an API to 400 sellers and shipping platforms for booking and tracking. Most call it politely. A few poll every shipment every few seconds, and last week one partner's retry loop took the database down for forty minutes.
Some partners pay for a higher tier, and a large partner may legitimately send a burst when a sale begins. The API runs on six instances behind a load balancer.
must_handle: A limit holds across all instances, near enough.
A partner over the limit is told clearly when to come back.
A burst from a paying partner at the start of a sale is allowed.
Booking a shipment matters more than polling one when the system is strained.
The limiter being down must not take the API down.
show_in_answer: Where the limit is checked, and where the counters live.
The response a partner gets, with its headers.
What the limiter does when its own store is unavailable.
What you would offer partners so that they need to poll less.
